summary: Ra is a Knizia auction game where players bid Sun tokens to win sets of tiles representing ancient Egyptian civilization elements, across three escalating epochs. It's tense and quick, with elegant push-your-luck decisions about when to trigger an auction versus keep drawing tiles.
praised: Elegant, tense bidding mechanism with real psychological depth
Fast-playing and easy to teach despite strategic richness
Strong theme integration through tile types (monuments, floods, civilizations)
criticised: Can feel swingy with disaster tiles wiping out progress
Bidding math and scoring can be fiddly for newcomers
Some randomness in tile draws affects auction quality

interaction.kind: closed-economy bidding where every sun spent is aimed at beating a specific rival
interaction.detail: Every auction is a direct bid against the other players for a shared, shrinking set of tiles, and a common tactic is bidding purely to deny an opponent a tile you don't even want yourself. Almost the entire game state — the tile pool and the timing of when an epoch ends — is shared and fought over rather than sitting on private boards.
interaction.said: "cutthroat auction", "you bid to deny, not just to win", "cruel when someone snipes your god tile" — Ra is repeatedly cited as one of the more directly combative auction games

subsystems: epoch-end tile tallying (Pharaohs, Niles/Floods, Civilizations, Monuments, Gold, God tiles)
scoring.how_you_win: After 3 epochs of auctioning tiles with suns, add up each epoch's Pharaoh/Nile/Civilization/Monument/Gold/God scoring plus leftover suns; the highest total wins.
sources: Nile and Flood tiles (points per Nile if a flood is held)
Golden God tile (bonus per monument type)
